subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw initially accept only canonical core readiness conditions and legacy-compatible projections, or commit now to the full provider, hosting-profile, CLI, artifact-identity, and release-conformance contract?
rationale: Implementation proof cannot determine which permanent availability, configuration, plugin API, CLI, and support promises maintainers intend to own.

options.title: Accept a staged foundation
options.body: Approve core conditions and compatibility projections first, then require separate acceptance and proof for broader surfaces.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve all proposed surfaces after the implementation defects, rebase, and upgrade evidence are complete.

options.title: Keep hosting composition external
options.body: Retain fixed Gateway readiness and leave supplemental hosting checks to hosts or plugins.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve core conditions and compatibility projections first, then require separate acceptance and proof for broader surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history directly connects this person to RFC acceptance policy, with runtime owners available for technical review.
